title: Budget 1:1 prep — procurement & run-rate notes
content:
Meeting: 1:1 prep with Marco (Finance lead) — focus: run-rate sanity check, upcoming procurement approvals, and immediate ask list
Date of meeting: 2025-11-11 (tentative)
Context/goal:
- Quick sync to align on 2026 run-rate assumptions and to get greenlight on two procurement asks (Dedicated GPU reserve + third-party monitoring).
- Leave with clear approval path and delegated next-steps; ideally sign-off on procurement requests that fall under our delegated authority.

High-level run-rate snapshot (rough numbers for discussion) — current month (Oct 2025) baseline:
- Monthly cash burn (ops + infra + people): ~$950k/mo (includes payroll, office, cloud, infra contracts)
- Annualized run-rate: ~$11.4M
- Infra-specific: ~38% of monthly burn (~$360k/mo) — split: cloud-hosted infra (public cloud consumables) 45%, Dedicated capacity/reserved contracts 35%, third-party SaaS & monitoring 20%
- Recent upward pressure: indexation on cloud rates + new dedicated capacity commitments for two enterprise customers (~+ $70k/month incremental if approved)

Questions I want answered in the 1:1:
1) Thresholds: confirm procurement approval thresholds for 2025-2026 (what can I sign vs. what needs your or legal/CPO sign-off). I think threshold: <=$50k finance manager sign-off, $50k-$200k CPO + finance, >$200k exec/board — confirm.
2) Capital vs Operating treatment: for the dedicated capacity reserved contract (12-month commit + onboarding fee), do we prefer to treat onboarding as CapEx for FY25 close? Impact on cash planning.
3) Prioritization: if we have to cut $100k/mo from run-rate, which infra lines should be first candidates? (options: delay dedicated commit, tighten autoscaling policies, push caching optimizations, delay non-critical monitoring upgrades)
4) Approval timeline: need rough ETA for procurement approval to meet vendor start dates (target deployment window mid-Dec 2025) — can we do an expedited review?

Procurement asks (two live asks, numbers are preliminary)
A) Dedicated GPU reserved pool (vendor: CloudHaven)
- Ask: 12-month reserved capacity for 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (shared for Dedicated tier customers)
- Cost: $120k/month reserved commit + one-time onboarding/integration fee $25k
- Rationale: predictable capacity for two enterprise deals (ensures latency SLOs), lower per-token cost vs on-demand, simplifies forecasting for Q1-Q2 2026.
- Risk/tradeoffs: increases fixed monthly run-rate; reduces flexibility if customer churn; requires commit alignment with sales coverage.
- Approval needed: finance + CPO sign-off for >$100k/mo commitment.
- Suggested approach: propose 6-month pilot with conversion to 12-month only after first invoice (negotiation with vendor).

B) Monitoring & Trace upgrade (vendor: TraceLens)
- Ask: move to enterprise tier for full distributed tracing and 12-month retention (needed for compliance + SRE efficiency)
- Cost: $18k/mo + $8k one-time migration/setup (total first-year ~$224k)
- Rationale: reduces mean time to detect (MTTD) and incident toil; supports upcoming Private deployments audit requirements.
- Approval needed: finance manager sign-off (under $50k) but want your explicit go/no-go because this is visibility-heavy.

Immediate prep items for me before the 1:1 (actionable)
- Pull detailed infra invoice breakdown for Oct & Sep (cloud, dedicated, SaaS) — status: in progress, Leah helping, ETA: 2025-11-06
- Create two-line financial memo for each procurement ask (one-pager for procurement) — ETA: 2025-11-08
- Draft procurement request forms and attach vendor contracts + SOWs (get legal checklist ready) — ETA: 2025-11-09
- Model run-rate sensitivity: show P&L impact of +$120k/mo vs -$100k/mo savings scenarios — ETA: 2025-11-07
- Prepare suggested negotiation levers for CloudHaven (6-month pilot, flexible early termination clause, performance SLAs) — ETA: 2025-11-08

Questions to ask Marco directly (scripted style to keep 1:1 efficient)
- "Confirm approval thresholds and who to loop in for >$100k/mo — is CPO + you sufficient or need legal + CEO?"
- "If we take the dedicated commit, are you OK treating onboarding as CapEx to smooth FY25 impact?"
- "Which infra line would you prioritize cutting if we need to shave $100k/mo quickly?"
- "Can we get an expedited review this month to meet vendor timeline (target mid-Dec)? If yes, who will own the exec summary for approval?"

Risks & Mitigations (to voice quickly)
- Risk: Committing to reserved capacity raises fixed costs and reduces agility if forecasts miss — Mitigation: pilot clause, link commit to specific enterprise deals with minimum revenue triggers.
- Risk: Monitoring upgrade adds Opex pressure — Mitigation: realize SRE efficiency savings (estimate 10% support FTE savings) and include those offsets in the model.
- Risk: Procurement timeline slips beyond vendor lead time — Mitigation: request provisional PO and parallel legal review; negotiate start date flexibility.

Follow-ups I want from Marco (if agreed in meeting)
- Quick sign-off email template or delegated approval authority for the $120k/mo commit (if Marco can OK, I can route to legal/CPO) — due: 2025-11-13
- Nominate a sales owner to lock the two enterprise deals to revenue recognition triggers tied to capacity commitment — due: 2025-11-13
- If approved, greenlight Leah to execute procurement paperwork and route to vendor — due: 2025-11-17

Notes & scratch ideas (brain dump)
- Could structure CloudHaven as "seasonal" commit with auto-scale buffer rather than fixed GPUs to reduce committed spend — ask vendor if convertible credits are available.
- Consider reclassifying part of TraceLens migration cost as a project expense funded from SRE discretionary spending to avoid expanding run-rate immediately.
- Longer term: evaluate model-level caching and query-side prefix caching to shave infra token costs. Short-term, a small targeted cache could reduce peak costs by ~10-15% per big customer request pattern (need ops experiment).

Attachments to prepare for meeting (what Marco will want to glance at)
- One-pager: "Dedicated capacity ask — CloudHaven" (with numbers & tradeoffs)
- One-pager: "TraceLens upgrade request"
- Cost model spreadsheet (sensitivity analysis) — link to spreadsheet in linked_artifacts
- Vendor contracts/SOWs (redlined version if legal already reviewed)

Open questions I need to answer before sending to procurement/legal
- Final negotiated monthly price and any early termination clauses (vendor negotiation team to confirm)
- Exact revenue triggers from sales that justify the dedicated commit (sales to confirm probability)
- Impact on gross margin if both asks are approved (need quick margin calc)

Draft email subject lines (short)
- "Request: approval needed — Dedicated GPU reserve (CloudHaven)"
- "Request: TraceLens enterprise upgrade — finance review"

Action items (simple checklist)
- [ ] Finalize infra invoice breakdown (Leah) — due 2025-11-06
- [ ] Complete two one-pagers (me) — due 2025-11-08
- [ ] Run sensitivity model (me + finance tools) — due 2025-11-07
- [ ] Legal to review vendor SOWs (loop legal) — request sent 2025-11-05
- [ ] Schedule exec summary if Marco says yes (owner: Marco or designate) — target 2025-11-13

Last-minute talking points (to keep meeting under 30 mins)
- Start with current run-rate headline (1-2 slides or lines)
- Present only the asks and alternatives (pilot, defer, scale)
- Ask for approval path & timelines, get commitments on who owns what
- End with next steps and dates

Notes to self after meeting (populate during 1:1)
- Record exact approval language Marco gives and any delegation (who signs what)
- Note any follow-up meetings (legal, sales, procurement) and owners

-- end of scratchpad --
